methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $22M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
RISE Robotics, founded by Arron Acosta and Blake Sessions, is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $22M+ to date. The valuation analysis considers a peer universe of 9 comparable companies—1 public and 8 private—spanning the robotics sector at seed through Series B stages, including Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, Generalist AI, and Bedrock Robotics.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $22M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A-to-subsequent-stage step-ups, implying a $44M valuation. Peer-median analysis examined four robotics companies at comparable or adjacent stages (Generalist AI at $2.0B, Bedrock Robotics at $1.8B, Dexterity at $1.6B, and Walden Robotics at $1.1B), establishing a median comparable valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce materially divergent results, with stage-progression implying $44M and peer-median implying $1.7B. Triangulation across both methods supports a range of $37M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $872M. The wide spread reflects stage and information asymmetry between early-stage capital deployment and comparable-company trading multiples. Key uncertainties include whether peer valuations reflect sustainable unit economics, the relevance of Series B valuations to pre-product-revenue Series A positioning, and the extent to which RISE's technology differentiation justifies premium-to-median positioning.
